newsitem.title: FRANCE: Israel's Barak urges halt to Russian N-help to Iran.
newsitem.headline: Israel's Barak urges halt to Russian N-help to Iran.

text.p: Israeli opposition leader Ehud Barak asked France on Monday to put pressure on Moscow to halt nuclear cooperation with Iran, fearing Tehran wanted to develop atomic weapons and long-range missiles.

Labour party leader Barak said after talks with Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin that a Russian plan to help construct a nuclear power plant in Iran "might influence or accelerate (Iran's) military programme."
He said he and Jospin also discussed what he called Russia's role in helping Tehran develop long-range missiles.
"I asked the prime minister to see whether he has any way to...try to influence them to delay as long as they can all such kind of participation," Barak said.

Russia has signed an $800 million deal with Iran to help complete the plant in the southern port of Bushehr despite U.S. objections that Tehran might use the technology to develop nuclear arms. Iran has repeatedly denied it wants nuclear bombs.
Barak said cooperation between Iran and Russia could threaten the Middle East, the supply of oil from the Gulf region and the vital interests of Israel.
He also said that Jospin and Barak also discussed stalled efforts for Middle East peace. Barak pleaded for continued aid for the Palestinians.
